Many many thanks for [your](/person/1019) most kind letter, and for telling me of the happy prospect before [Dora](/person/968)[^1] . . . I have asked [Mrs. Wilson](/person/1539) to send on to you a letter of [Bishop Patteson](/person/1155)’s, which I think you will feel refreshed by reading; please send it on to [Miss Anne Mackenzie](/person/930). You are so very kind, and it would be very delightful to make one in the migration; but I have only seen [Miss Dyson](/person/464) for a day since her sorrow, and not at all since mine,[^2] and the meeting at Testwood has become such an institution that I could not fail in it, so I must wait until you are at Brighstone again, and I have always had a wish to see that in spring. I have just returned from [Lady Seaton](/person/314)’s It is a [house](/place/126) of shadows and memories to me.


[^1]: Dora Frances Moberly’s had become engaged to the Rev. Charles Martin, whom she married 14 September 1869.
[^2]: Mary Anne Dyson\'s sister-in-law [Elizabeth Dyson](/person/462) (with whom she had lived at Crookham since her brother’s death) had died in the first quarter of 1868, and CMY\'s [mother](/person/1606) had died on 28 September 1868.
